input: Under /uploads there are files with various extensions. Write a script that: 1) For each file, determines its extension and moves it into a subdirectory named after that extension (e.g., .txt files go to /uploads/txt/, .csv files go to /uploads/csv/). Create the subdirectories as needed. 2) Print each move as 'moved: FILENAME -> EXTENSION_DIR/'. 3) After all moves, print a summary of how many files per extension as 'EXT: N files'. Handle the case where a file has no extension by putting it in /uploads/other/.

transcript.final_response:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

UPLOAD_DIR=/uploads
declare -A counts=()

while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
  name=${file##*/}

  # Treat a lone dotfile (such as .bashrc) and names ending in a dot
  # as having no extension. Otherwise, use the text after the final dot.
  if [[ $name == *.* && $name != .* && $name != *. ]]; then
    ext=${name##*.}
  elif [[ $name == .*.* && $name != *. ]]; then
    ext=${name##*.}
  else
    ext=other
  fi

  mkdir -p -- "$UPLOAD_DIR/$ext"
  mv -- "$file" "$UPLOAD_DIR/$ext/"
  printf 'moved: %s -> %s/\n' "$name" "$ext"
  ((counts["$ext"] += 1))
done < <(find "$UPLOAD_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -print0)

for ext in "${!counts[@]}"; do
  printf '%s: %d files\n' "$ext" "${counts[$ext]}"
done | sort
```

Save it as a Bash script and run it. It processes files directly inside `/uploads`, placing extensionless files in `/uploads/other/`.
